item.title: UN inquiry member says some genocide claims against Israel unverified as Gaza reports population growth
item.description: Experts say Palestinian Ministry of Health mortality figures contradict famine declarations and genocide allegations as Gaza's population grew in 2025.
item.content:encoded:
The allegations of genocide against Israel took more hits this week following the reported admission by a senior member of the U.N. Commission of Inquiry on Israel that claims had not been independently verified. This comes as the Palestinian Ministry of Health data shows Gaza’s population grew in 2025.

Critics say the accusations fueled antisemitism around the world and that those pushing the genocide claims — including major international media outlets — need to be made accountable for their words.

In Sept. 2025, the Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem and Israel (COI) released a report stating that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza since Oct. 2023. In the report, the COI cited an article from the Guardian stating that 83% of Gazans killed in the conflict were civilians.

ISRAEL SLAMS UN REPORT AS 'POLITICAL BLOOD LIBEL' FOR ALLEGING DELIBERATE TARGETING OF PALESTINIAN CHILDREN

Following the release of data from the COI commissioner, Chris Sidoti, in an interview last week reported by JNS and posted on X  was asked whether the COI had independently established that the remainder of Palestinians said to be killed in the fighting were civilians, Sidoti said, "No, we didn’t because we don’t have that information…We literally do not know, nor does anybody else know, including the IDF, how many militants were there." 

The former chair of the committee, Navay Pillay, was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize last week.

The Palestinian MOH Health Information Unit recently released statistics on overall mortality in Gaza for 2025. This is the first update to include non-violent deaths since 2022, prior to the outbreak of conflict following the terror attacks of Oct. 7, 2023.

UNICEF GAZA FINDINGS ‘COMPLETELY SHATTERS’ STARVATION CLAIMS AGAINST ISRAEL, STATE DEPT SAYS

The MOH reported that 24,650 deaths were registered in 2025, with 18,085 (73.4%) being males and 6,565 (26.6%) being females. 70.1% of deaths, or 17,286 cases, were attributed to direct targeting in the war.

The MOH also reported 50,227 live births in 2025. Fox News Digital reached out to officials at the ministry but did not get a response by press time.

Elliot Malin, president at Stratos Council, told Fox News Digital that the MOH data is further evidence against accusations of genocide. With the number of live births in 2025 far greater than the number of deaths, Malin says it is "very hard for us to infer the intent of Israel was to destroy Palestinians in Gaza to a substantial portion."

"We’re not seeing a population under threat. We are seeing that it is actually able to sustain itself," Malin said. He took issue with the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) declaration last year that famine had reached Gaza in the summer of 2025. Malin said that "if the population is sustaining and growing through this, what they call a famine, it indicates that there is enough caloric intake to sustain the population."

Gabriel Epstein, senior policy associate at Israel Policy Forum, also told Fox News Digital that widespread allegations of genocide are not supported by the MOH report. First, the report "absolutely" demonstrates population growth in 2025, according to Epstein, who added it would "be surprising" if the population of Gaza, "one of the youngest…in the world," was not growing.

While he says that it is impossible to discern the actual rate of population growth given factors like emigration and immigration, Epstein said that "the argument that we would need to make to say that there was negative population growth in 2025 would be to more than double the number of both violent and non-violent deaths."

SIGN UP FOR ANTISEMITISM EXPOSED NEWSLETTER

Andrew Fox, senior associate fellow at the Henry Jackson Society, told Fox News Digital that "the data now shows that there was no famine in Gaza." He said that the allegations play into "the ages-old blood libel of Jews killing children and undoubtedly stoked the global fires of antisemitism. Agencies and the media who shared these false allegations have blood on their hands."

Epstein said that the latest MOH data is strong proof against the statements from external organizations who used estimates and ratios of non-violent deaths from other conflict zones to suppose that the MOH’s ongoing count of the death toll in Gaza was inaccurate, and that deaths had likely reached multiple hundreds of thousands. These estimated figures were largely used to drive the narrative that Israel was committing genocide in Gaza. He said that current MOH figures "really eliminate the possibility that there is a much higher death toll driven by non-violent or non-trauma deaths."

He noted that comparing the latest report with ongoing MOH data on overall casualties throughout the war shows that the MOH was not "missing the vast, vast majority of [malnutrition-related] deaths you would have needed to be missing to justify the IPC’s assessment" that famine had reached parts of Gaza in summer 2025.

The IPC did not respond to Fox News Digital’s questions about how new information impacts its prior declaration of famine.

NOBEL PEACE PRIZE AWARDED TO UN JURIST WHO ACCUSED ISRAEL OF COMMITTING GENOCIDE IN GAZA

In the MOH’s favor, Epstein said that the current tranche of figures supports a real attempt at honest accounting from the health organization, which was accused of inflating civilian casualties – particularly those of women and children– during the early days of the war.

In its latest report, however, the MOH does not distinguish how many terrorists were among those killed in the conflict. In fact, it states that, "The number of deaths among males was approximately 4.9 times the number of deaths among females within this group – attributed principally to the direct targeting of working-age men during military operations."

IDF PUSHES BACK ON CLAIM THAT IT TARGETS JOURNALISTS IN GAZA, SAYS 170 WERE PART OF TERROR GROUPS, INCLUDING HAMAS

A spokesperson from the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) told Fox News Digital that, "The IDF targets terrorists and military objectives, not civilians based on their age or gender. The fact that more military-age men are disproportionately among those eliminated is consistent with the fact that terrorist organizations are predominantly composed of men in this age group. It does not demonstrate that the IDF targets individuals because they are men or of a certain age." 

The spokesperson added that, "Targets are selected based on their military nature or an individual’s involvement in terrorist organizations or participation in hostilities, in accordance with international law and IDF directives. Unlike Hamas, which deliberately targets Israeli civilians, the IDF takes all feasible precautions to mitigate harm to civilians and operates under a structured targeting framework designed to ensure the identification of lawful military objectives. "

Epstein also pushed back against the MOH claim that working-aged men are being purposefully targeted. Epstein said that "military-aged men aren't appearing disproportionately because the IDF was targeting military-aged men as such, but because the vast majority of militants come from that range." He said that "Gaza is unique in how heavily militarized its male population is."

Epstein added that available 2025 data does not support the claim that the IDF acted with the intent to cause harm to the population. Not only do the Oct. 7, 2023 attacks and hybridization of civilian and military structures in Gaza provide a rationale for military targeting, Epstein emphasized that the IDF has taken numerous mitigation measures to avoid civilian casualties.

Requests for comment to the Palestinian Ministry of Health were not returned by press time.

item.title: NBA and WNBA back Lean In Girls program that tells facilitators not to call participants 'girls'
item.description: The NBA and WNBA back Sheryl Sandberg's Lean In Girls, whose handbook tells adults not to call participants "girls" and covers gender identity.
item.content:encoded:
The NBA and WNBA have spent more than a decade working with Sheryl Sandberg's Lean In organization, a relationship that has expanded to include promoting a leadership program for girls as young as 11.

There's just one problem: A handbook for adults running the program tells them not to address the group as "girls."

Yes, Lean In Girls, which the NBA and WNBA say they're "proud to support," includes guidance for working with participants who may be exploring their gender identity. Its facilitator handbook encourages children to share their pronouns and instructs adults to use gender-neutral language.

WNBPA ISSUES STATEMENT EMBRACING DIVERSITY AND INCLUSION AMID TRANS ATHLETE DEBATE IN WOMEN'S SPORTS

The handbook also discusses "social power" and "active allyship," teaching facilitators how to help young participants recognize and challenge societal biases.

So, how much of the curriculum did the NBA and WNBA review before deciding to support the program?

The NBA's 2022-23 Social Impact Report stated that the WNBA had worked with Lean In for eight years, airing public service announcements during the playoffs to promote the value of girls and women in sports.

Those early campaigns focused on gender equality and encouraging men to support women. By 2024, the partnership included Lean In Girls, a program designed specifically for children.

That year, the leagues teamed up with WNBA star Aliyah Boston for a promotional campaign encouraging girls to reject stereotypes and embrace their "leadership superpowers."

On April 20, 2026, the NBA published a video describing Lean In Girls as a "free, school-ready" program backed by both leagues. Promotional ads for Lean In also air during WNBA broadcasts.

The WNBA also teamed up with Flau'jae Johnson, with Lean In's website declaring that Johnson and the league were proud to support the initiative.

Lean In says the free program is designed for girls ages 11-15 and can be used in schools and community organizations.

OutKick obtained a 2023 Lean In Girls Facilitator Handbook through Courage Is A Habit, a parental-rights organization that previously investigated the program.

The handbook describes Lean In Girls as a program developed for girls and young teenagers who "identify with the girlhood experience." The program includes leadership activities involving goal-setting, confidence and dealing with failure. One section, titled "Gender inclusion," explains that some participants may be exploring their gender identity or feel uncomfortable with the label "girl."

"When you greet your group or refer to them as a whole, avoid calling them 'girls' or 'guys,'" the handbook states.

Instead, facilitators are encouraged to use terms such as "everyone," "folks," "leaders" and "team." The handbook also encourages participants to share their pronouns, though it cautions against making the practice mandatory, and suggests substituting they/them pronouns into fictional scenarios.

NIKE-LINKED COACHINGHER PROGRAM FACES SCRUTINY OVER GENDER BIAS TRAINING AND DEFINITION OF GIRLS

Another section instructs facilitators to consider how people's identities affect their "social power." According to Lean In Girls, adults, wealthy people and able-bodied individuals generally have more power than teenagers, people living in poverty and people with disabilities.

The handbook also encourages facilitators to create a "brave space" where teenagers can "contend with injustice" and practice "active allyship."

During a February 2026 webinar hosted by the American School Counselor Association, Lean In Girls official Kelly Meredith described an updated 15-session program with four sections. She said Part 3 addresses overcoming bias and barriers, while Part 4 focuses on allyship.

OutKick requested the current curriculum, including Parts 3 and 4, to establish what material facilitators are being given today. Lean In initially directed OutKick to another email inbox. The organization did not provide the materials or respond to subsequent follow-up emails.

Records obtained by OutKick show that Santa Clara Unified School District brought Lean In Girls into Buchser Middle School and explored expanding it to four other middle schools.

At the district's Spring 2025 Equity Convening, Buchser counselor Brenda Goldstein and vice principal Gilbert Montiel presented Lean In Girls as a "Tier 2 Intervention," a designation for targeted student support.

The school said eighth-grade girls were struggling with social connections, confidence and negative social messages. Officials reviewed academic performance, attendance and discipline records, along with weekly Panorama check-ins, when evaluating the need for the program.

According to the district presentation, recruitment included applications with essay questions and interviews. Academic data and Panorama check-in histories also factored into the recruitment process, as did "diversity."

The school's stated objectives included helping girls examine gender and cultural stereotypes, understand their identities and recognize barriers to leadership.

The district later developed plans for programs at five middle schools. One presentation proposed a "formal partnership with Lean In Girls as their first public school partner."

A planning document shows that several schools intended to use only Parts 1 and 2 of the curriculum. The records don't explain why Parts 3 and 4 were left out or whether officials reviewed those sections.

The records confirm that Buchser implemented the program, but don't establish which lessons students received or whether the planned expansion happened.

Recruitment materials provided by the district promoted confidence-building and leadership activities, including confronting bias and challenging stereotypes. The records don't establish whether parents were told about the facilitator handbook's guidance on gender identity, pronouns and nonbinary participants.

OutKick asked Santa Clara Unified officials which schools ultimately implemented the program and whether they reviewed Parts 3 and 4. OutKick also asked whether participation was voluntary and whether affirmative parental consent was required.

In an Oct. 12, 2026, email, district official Mark Schiel acknowledged the questions and said he would attempt to provide answers, noting that some staff members were unavailable because classes were not in session. OutKick extended the district's response deadline as a courtesy.

The district did not provide answers by the extended deadline.

In July, OutKick reported that the WNBA selected Girls in the Game as a beneficiary of its All-Star Game charitable initiative. The organization, which the league supported as part of its effort to keep girls involved in sports, said on its website that it was "moving beyond the binary of 'girl'" and welcomed gender-expansive participants.

OutKick asked the WNBA whether it knew about that language before selecting the organization and whether biological males could participate in its girl-centered programs. Neither the WNBA nor Girls in the Game answered those questions.

For this story, OutKick contacted the NBA, WNBA and Lean In Girls to ask what the leagues reviewed before endorsing the program and who approved the relationship. The inquiry also asked whether league officials were aware of the gender-identity guidance. The leagues were asked whether they provide financial support and what information was given to players featured in promotional campaigns. Lean In Girls was asked to provide its current curriculum and explain what materials it shared with the leagues.

OutKick has been seeking answers and curriculum materials from Lean In since August 2026. The NBA and WNBA were first contacted on Oct. 9. None of the three organizations provided substantive answers by the Oct. 13 deadline.

The NBA publicly described Lean In Girls as "school-ready" and put its name behind the program. Explaining whether anyone at the league actually reviewed the material before doing so shouldn't be nearly as difficult.

item.title: Talarico dismisses past comments about God and gender as 'provocative' while invoking Charlie Kirk
item.description: James Talarico faced a Christian voter at a CNN town hall who questioned his faith over past comments calling God "non-binary" and citing the Bible.
item.content:encoded:
Texas’ Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico dismissed his past comments referring to God as "nonbinary" and using the Bible to justify his pro-choice stance on abortion during a Wednesday night CNN town hall.

Participating in a "Jubilee"-style town hall in which voters confronted him one-on-one, Talarico met with a fellow Christian from Texas who pressed him on his past statements.

"You've said some concerning things in the past kind of related to faith and social issues. Things such as God is nonbinary, questions about how many genders there really are and your justifications using the Bible for abortion," Sarah Gardner, a small business owner, said to Talarico.

TALARICO SAYS HE 'HATES CHRISTIANITY' IN UNEARTHED INTERVIEW WITH TRANSGENDER 'LATINX' THEOLOGIAN

"And so, I think that's led a lot of Christian voters to question the authenticity of your faith. And I wanted to ask you a very direct question. Do you believe that the Bible is the absolute source of truth and God's final authoritative word, even when our culture says otherwise?" she asked.

"Yes," Talarico replied. "And I think it's important to remember that even the early church, the disciples who actually knew Jesus of Nazareth, the early church, we often talk about as a singular body when, in reality, was more like early churches because there was a lot of disagreement, there was a lot of debate."

TED CRUZ, CONSERVATIVES RESPOND AFTER TALARICO CRITICIZES BIBLE-RELATED EDUCATION IN SCHOOLS AS 'PROPAGANDA'

Talarico then went on to explain his past comments as being "provocative," drawing a parallel to his own interpretation of scripture to Charlie Kirk’s.

"I actually want to clarify a few of the things that you said, because I know that this has been used in these attack ads all over the state," he began.

UNEARTHED CLIP SHOWS TALARICO CALLING PARENTS 'ABUSIVE' FOR DENYING CHILDREN'S GENDER IDENTITY

"The first comment about God not being defined by gender, when I said that I was being provocative. And I want to admit that and come clean about that. But I think what I was saying is actually not controversial theologically. The idea that we can't define God using human categories, not only did I say that, but the late Charlie Kirk said that, the late Pope Benedict said that. And so, yes, I was doing it, maybe in an annoying way, I can admit that," he said.

Talarico, a state senator in Texas, previously said, "God is both masculine and feminine, and everything in between. God is nonbinary. In Genesis 1:26, God speaks of God's self in the plural, saying, 'Let us make man in our image.'"

EXPERT TEARS APART TALARICO'S VIRAL CLAIM HIS AGENDA IS BASED ON JESUS'S TEACHINGS: 'BUTCHERING THE BIBLE'

He also dismissed the notion that the Bible refers to abortion.

"The idea that there is a set Christian orthodoxy on the issue of abortion is just not rooted in Scripture," he said during a 2025 appearance on The Joe Rogan Experience.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Talarico campaign for further comment.

item.title: Trump announces Montana 'super range' at midterm rally for Pentagon to test advanced war technology
item.description: President Donald Trump announced at a Kalispell rally that the Pentagon will build a military super range in Montana for hypersonic weapons testing.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump delivered "a little breaking news" to supporters at a midterm campaign rally in Montana on Wednesday, announcing that the Pentagon would establish a new military "super range" in the state to test cutting-edge weapons and warfare technology.

The president said the range would support testing of potential autonomous weapons, space and electronic warfare technology, and supersonic and hypersonic systems, positioning Montana to play a greater role in the development of America's next-generation military capabilities.

"I'm pleased to inform you and announce that right here in Montana, the Department of War is going to establish a new super range for testing advanced weapons and technologies," Trump told supporters gathered at Majestic Valley Arena in Kalispell.

TRUMP PENTAGON LAUNCHES COMPETITION FOR AMERICA'S NEXT GREAT MILITARY BASE

Trump suggested the project had been highly sought after elsewhere in the country.

"The rest of our country maybe won't be thrilled because a lot of other people wanted it also," Trump said.

The president also credited persistent lobbying from Montana's Republican lawmakers, joking that Sen. Tim Sheehy had repeatedly pressed him to bring the project to the state.

"You're getting it, everybody, will you please leave me alone?" Trump quipped. "Leave me alone, Tim. Tim Sheehy would drive me crazy."

The announcement places Montana at the center of a proposed military testing initiative involving some of the Pentagon's most sophisticated emerging technologies.

Hypersonic weapons, which can travel at least five times the speed of sound, are among the advanced military capabilities under development by the Pentagon, according to the Government Accountability Office. The War Department has also identified autonomous systems and electronic warfare capabilities as areas of strategic importance.

ELON MUSK LANDS NEW TRUMP ADMINISTRATION ROLE IN SHAPING FUTURE OF AMERICAN WARFARE

Trump did not specify where in Montana the new range would be located, how much the project would cost or when testing operations would begin.

"Montana will help ensure the American military always reigned supreme," the president told the crowd.

Trump made the announcement during his second campaign rally of the day and third stop on a Western swing aimed at supporting Republican candidates ahead of the midterm elections.

The president appeared in Montana's 1st Congressional District to campaign for House candidate Aaron Flint and Senate candidate Kurt Alme, after holding a rally in Arizona earlier Wednesday. He also campaigned in Alaska on Tuesday.

item.title: Lost piece of Jesus' world emerges after 2,000 years in extraordinary discovery
item.description: The Israel Antiquities Authority uncovered a 2,000-year-old aqueduct near Jerusalem that a biblical scholar believes has links to Jesus and early Christians.
item.content:encoded:
A 2,000-year-old aqueduct was recently uncovered near Jerusalem — and it likely supplied water used by Jesus and his disciples, according to a biblical scholar.

Archaeologists unearthed a roughly 984-foot section of the ancient waterway south of Kibbutz Ramat Rachel — which once carried water from Solomon's Pools near Bethlehem to Jerusalem's Temple Mount.

The discovery was announced by the Israel Antiquities Authority (IAA) on Oct. 11, following excavations ahead of a planned residential development.

MASSIVE 2,000-YEAR-OLD DISCOVERY FROM TIME OF JESUS EMERGES REMARKABLY INTACT

Originally constructed during the Hasmonean period, the aqueduct remained in intermittent use until about a century ago, the IAA said.

The waterway relied on gravity to transport water to the Second Temple complex, the center of Jewish religious life at the time, where it was used for ritual purification and cleaning up after sacrifices.

The Second Temple complex was also the setting of the biblical account of Jesus cleansing the Temple, during which he overturned the tables of money changers and drove out merchants.

The Lower Aqueduct was "probably built in the time of the Hasmonean kings to supply water to Jerusalem," according to excavation directors Benyamin Storchan, Gil Freid and Rotem Cohen of the Israel Antiquities Authority.

ARCHAEOLOGISTS UNCOVER 'MYSTERIOUS' ANCIENT TUNNEL NEAR BIBLICAL KINGDOM OF JUDAH SITE IN JERUSALEM

"The aqueduct runs about 21 km [13 miles] from Solomon's Pools, south of Bethlehem, to Jerusalem," the directors said in a statement.

"Along most of the route, the water flowed along a very gentle gradient, dropping just one meter [3.3 feet] in elevation per kilometer [0.6 miles]."

The aqueduct will be preserved and incorporated into the main entrance of the planned residential development, allowing visitors to see the ancient engineering firsthand.

UNEXPECTED ANCIENT COMPLEX EMERGES NEAR BIBLICAL CITY LINKED TO JONAH AND ST PETER

"The engineering that was required to make this work is really amazing," Douglas Estes, an associate professor of religion at New College of Florida, told Fox News Digital.

Estes said the aqueduct's construction reflected Jerusalem's prominence in the ancient world, comparing the significance of such infrastructure to the construction of modern skyscrapers.

"The Hasmoneans, Jewish rulers, were building this aqueduct at the same time that the Romans were building their aqueduct that carried water to the Temple of Jupiter on Capitoline Hill," Estes said.

"We think of Rome as being the power in the Mediterranean at the time, and we think of Jerusalem as being a small capital of the city-state, but they were actually advancing in technology at the same time and building their aqueducts together."

Beyond its impressive engineering, Estes said the discovery also sheds light on religious practices in ancient Jerusalem and their connections to early Christianity.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Estes said the aqueduct's water was used for both practical and religious purposes, including cleaning up after sacrifices and performing purification rituals at the Temple Mount.

Estes said he was "confident" that Jesus, his disciples and other early Christians would have used water supplied by the aqueduct, although direct archaeological evidence of their individual use has not been established.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The system, which relied on fresh, or "living" water, also carries symbolic significance for Christians, Estes said.

"It brought living water from Bethlehem to the Temple Mount, so that sanctification could take place after sacrifice," Estes said.

"For Christians, Jesus is the living water, and therefore … he came from Bethlehem as the living [water] to become the temple, to make the sacrifice of himself for all people."

Estes added, "There is a rich symbolism that we see here in this aqueduct."

item.title: Chinese national accused of poisoning cancer researcher had laptops seized while fleeing U.S.: cops
item.description: University of Wyoming student Aili Wang was allegedly caught on surveillance footage poisoning a colleague's mug with acrylamide, a neurotoxin.
item.content:encoded:
A University of Wyoming student was arrested after police say she tried to poison a colleague, then attempted to flee to China when officers questioned her.

Aili Wang, 32, was questioned by campus police after surveillance cameras set up by a coworker experiencing medical symptoms allegedly caught her rinsing his mug with liquid from her own cup on Oct. 1, according to a University of Wyoming police affidavit, which added that she was seen on camera "taking photos and manipulating notebooks."

Wang didn't get along with the coworker, who wasn't named in court documents. Surveillance footage allegedly showed Wang searching through the victim's desk; the victim specialized in disease treatment technology, work similar to what she had done in China.

COVID SCIENTIST ACCUSED OF USING CHATGPT IN ALLEGED POISONING PLOT AGAINST RIVAL

The liquid was identified as acrylamide, a chemical that can "cause a number of health problems, including cancer," according to the American Cancer Society. According to authorities, Wang purchased the chemical through eBay. It was discovered after the victim's wife ran a test on water taken from the coffee maker he used to brew tea.

When questioned by campus police on Oct. 5, Wang said she "had not used acrylamide in years," according to court documents. She was arrested one day later on Oct. 6 at Los Angeles International Airport and prosecutors allege she was attempting to return to China, where she is from.

CHINESE NATIONAL ARRESTED AT JFK AFTER ALLEGEDLY PHOTOGRAPHING US MILITARY AIRCRAFT AT NEBRASKA BASE

When she was arrested, Wang was found with "multiple laptops, multiple portable external digital storage devices, related accessories, physical records and written materials," according to a request from prosecutors to increase her $200,000 bond after being extradited back to Wyoming. Her bond was increased to $1.5 million cash-only.

The affidavit states that the victim's work was federally funded research involving "new technology for cancer, neurological and genetic disease treatment," and stated Wang didn't have a reason to be going through his desk.

OHIO STATE PAYS $2.1M SETTLEMENT AS IT ADMITS RESEARCHER HAD ‘INAPPROPRIATE FOREIGN AFFILIATIONS’ TO CHINA

Mark Gomelsky, a microbiology professor at the University of Wyoming who oversaw both graduate students, told Fox News Digital it has been a "horrifying and surreal experience."

He told The Associated Press, "It’s been disheartening, to say the least, to see that one of your student’s life is in jeopardy and another student may be responsible for that."

"That was one of the worst shocks in my professional career," Gomelsky said.

According to Gomelsky, the victim is a highly successful student from Vietnam. Gomelsky said Wang did not pass her first dissertation defense and became envious of her colleague's achievement in finding a way to use bacteria to deliver RNA to human cells.

The professor said the victim suddenly experienced extreme tiredness and an inability to sleep shortly after attending a prestigious conference in August.

Gomelsky said the victim is still experiencing symptoms from the alleged poisoning, which include not being able to focus.

"Acrylamide is a neurotoxin that cannot be neutralized so it stays in neurons and basically kills them. So it’s unclear if he’ll fully recover or not," Gomelsky said.

item.title: Two iconic American baseball equipment companies are now owned by a Chinese company associated with the CCP
item.description: Wilson and Louisville Slugger, two of baseball's most iconic American brands, are now controlled by Anta Sports, a Chinese company with deep CCP ties.
item.content:encoded:
It's the American pastime. It's as American as apple pie.

For nearly 200 years, from 20 years before the Civil War, baseball has been associated with the United States. One of our first unique sports, that's been so beloved since its inception that still, even in the modern era, it overwhelmingly leads all domestic sports leagues in total attendance.

Baseball has been a unifying force since its inception, leading to some of the most iconic moments in U.S. sports history. Jackie Robinson breaking the color barrier and helping pave the way for other integration in domestic sports competitions. Willie Mays' catch in center field at the Polo Grounds. Babe Ruth's "called shot," which became a national legend starting in 1932.

MAJOR LEAGUE BASEBALL HAS A HUGE PROBLEM BREWING FOR THE 2026-2027 OFFSEASON

Star baseball players like Ted Williams left the sport in the middle of their careers to join the armed forces in World War II. Lou Gehrig's iconic speech to the Yankee Stadium crowd regarding his ALS diagnosis, "Today, I consider myself the luckiest man on the face of the earth."

Yes, the NFL has become the most popular sports league in the country, but nothing inspires the level of regional fan dedication like baseball. Little League is something of a rite of passage for young boys, and virtually every town in America has a baseball field.

It'd be reasonable to assume, then, that the iconic companies who supply baseball equipment at both the youth and professional level would be, well, American. It'd be reasonable, yes, but unfortunately, it'd also be inaccurate. And that reality is an unfortunate symptom of a much bigger and broader problem.

Two of the most prolific baseball equipment manufacturers, known for over 100 years of making gloves and bats, are Wilson and Louisville Slugger. While many competitors have entered the space in recent years, a look across any baseball field, with children or adults playing, and you'll find Wilson gloves and equipment, and hitters using Louisville Slugger bats.

A number of star players, including Ronald Acuna Jr., Kyle Schwarber, Pete Crow-Armstrong, and Will Smith, use Louisville Slugger bats. Clayton Kershaw famously used a Wilson glove his entire career.

Louisville Slugger was founded in the 1880s, Wilson sporting goods just before the start of World War I. They're American companies, making sporting equipment for the most American of sports. Or at least, they were. Now? Both are owned by a company with deep ties to the Chinese Communist Party. Seriously.

STEPH CURRY SIGNS 10-YEAR DEAL WITH CHINESE BRAND LI-NING, RAISING QUESTIONS ABOUT NBA'S TIES TO CHINA

For most of the company's existence, Louisville Slugger was owned and operated by the Hillerich & Bradsby Company, founded in the 1800s to make baseball equipment. In 2015 though, the family-owned business, still in the Hillerich family, was essentially forced to sell.

CEO John A. Hillerich IV said at the time that he had effectively no choice because they weren't able to compete with mega, multinational companies that had entered the equipment space with much larger resources. They sold to Wilson, another company that started as a family business before being sold to an international conglomerate.

As far back as 1989, Wilson was sold to Amer Sports, a Finnish multinational manufacturer of athletic equipment. But in 2018, Amer itself was purchased by one of the largest athletic companies on earth, Anta Sports. Anta, a Chinese company, then by extension took over control of Wilson and Louisville Slugger.

So who is Anta? Well, that's where the symptom of a bigger and broader problem comes into play.

Anta is a relatively new business, founded in 1991, with the express goal of becoming the biggest athletic company on earth. Already, they're the third largest such company behind only Nike and Adidas. How'd they get so big, so quickly? The typical story of Chinese businesses: they copied Western companies.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Because manufacturing in China is so much cheaper than other countries, thanks to their poor working conditions and low wages, companies began outsourcing production to Anta, and companies like it, as globalization ramped up in recent decades. And as a BBC story on the company explains, they take advantage by uh, borrowing, "fundamentals of managing the business," as well as design and development techniques.

So companies like Nike hire Anta to make their shoes, designed and developed in the United States, in order to save some money, and Anta then copies their designs, manufacturing tolerances, and processes. Sure enough, a few years later, Anta is far outselling Nike in their home market, opening up stores in Los Angeles, and the "saving money" backfires when international sales tank.

Anta, with their global ambition to become the dominant company in the athletic space, expanded to buy Amer, and now by extension, controls two of the most iconic American businesses. That's bad enough, but Anta is heavily integrated with the Chinese Communist Party.

As just one example, in 2019, the company suspended contract negotiations with the NBA after then-Houston Rockets GM Daryl Morey retweeted support of pro-democracy protests in Hong Kong. In 2021, Anta's billionaire owner announced that the company would donate $1.2 billion worth of shares to a "charity."

That charity, was, like virtually any large business in China, intimately connected to the CCP. A Forbes report from the time explained it, "As inherently Chinese companies, both ANTA and LiNing will thus likely remain loyal to the CCP's understanding of human rights, especially as their domestic revenues dwarf anything they earn abroad."

Does that sound like the type of company that Americans want buying into youth and professional sports?

It's easy to wonder how this happened; how did it get to a point where a company indistinguishable from the Chinese government is controlling the manufacturing of equipment used by millions of young and professional athletes. But as is all too often the case, it's a series of inevitable consequences to short-sided thinking.

Companies that wanted to cut costs in the 1990s and 2000s by outsourcing to China are now being replaced in one of the world's largest markets by businesses that copied their designs and methodologies. Ultimately harming their bottom line in 2026 and beyond. Nike, in particular, has seen its share price collapse.

Smaller family businesses have little hope of vying against well-heeled multinational corporations, who themselves are eventually swallowed up by Chinese outlets able to outcompete on costs and local forcing functions.

Anta might be allowing Wilson and Louisville to operate as they did before. But for how long? How many other legendary companies will face a similarly depressing fate? Much like iconic businesses in London, such as Harrods, that are now owned by Middle Eastern sovereign wealth funds, American traditions are slowly being swallowed up by companies and countries that often have views antithetical to the US and the West.

Given how Major League Baseball celebrated America's 250th anniversary early this year, it's a miracle Anta hasn't pulled Wilson and Louisville out of protest. Maybe we shouldn't give them any ideas.

item.title: FIRST ON FOX: Wikipedia’s editorial safeguards failed to correct antisemitic content, ADL says
item.description: ADL CEO Jonathan Greenblatt says 91% of a banned Wikipedia editor's biased edits on Israel, Hamas and October 7 pages remain live and unchecked.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: More than a year after the Anti-Defamation League (ADL) uncovered a group of at least 30 Wikipedia editors seemingly coordinating to add anti-Israel bias, misleading information and antisemitic narratives, the group says the online encyclopedia has yet to edit or remove much of the concerning content.

"We had expected that these editors would be removed. We had expected that their edits would have been reversed. We expected that new policies would have implemented. Almost nothing has changed," ADL CEO and National Director Jonathan Greenblatt told Fox News Digital.

In the 2025 report, "Editing for Hate," the ADL raised several issues, including a "coordinated campaign" of manipulation of Wikipedia content related to Israel, Palestine and similar topics. Additionally, the organization said it found pro-Hamas perspectives informing Arabic-language content on those same topics. The group of 30 editors, according to the ADL, were more active than comparable groups "by a factor of at least two."

WIKIPEDIA CO-FOUNDER SAYS LEFT'S 'RELENTLESS' TAKEOVER OF MASS MEDIA RUINED THE WEBSITE HE HELPED BUILD

Wikipedia's community banned some of the editors from the topic area or from the site entirely following the 2025 report. However, the ADL claims the issues that it flagged were not resolved with the restrictions on those named in its previous report.

In its 2026 report, "Damage Done: Wikipedia Leaves Biased Edits Unchecked Despite Editor Bans," the ADL stated that "no banned editor's body of work has been systemically reviewed to determine which edits should be corrected." The organization found that across seven articles reviewed for its 2026 report, six of which are "flagship pages," 91% of a banned editor's edits were still live.

"A topic ban is great in theory, but in practice, if you're not doing it, if you aren't really taking action, there's really no ban at all," Greenblatt told Fox News Digital. "It's as if you had an individual who was spraying graffiti on the walls of public buildings. You might arrest that individual, but you don't erase or clean up the graffiti. You still leave it on the public institutions. Like, no one would do that in the real world. I don't know why that is acceptable as a practice on Wikipedia."

An account known as Iskandar323, which was part of the group of 30 editors documented in the 2025 report, serves as a case study of what has happened in the time since then. The ADL found that the account had a years-long editing history that showed a notable uptick following Hamas' Oct. 7 attacks in Israel.

The account, according to the ADL, made 485 edits across six articles, 225 of which came after the Hamas massacre, including 85 that were made in Oct. 2023. The ADL noted that the six pages that were edited "are among the highest-trafficked English-language Wikipedia entries on the topic." The pages were "Israel," "Gaza war," "October 7 attacks," "Hamas," "Zionism" and "Jews."

NEW YORK TIMES ISSUES CORRECTION, DELETES LINE QUESTIONING IF ISRAELIS WERE VICTIMS OF OCT 7 TERROR ATTACK

Wikipedia's Arbitration Committee (ArbCom) discussed Iskandar323's conduct in public proceedings. ArbCom found that Iskandar323 "engaged in disruptive behavior in the PIA topic area, including consistently non-neutral editing." The account was given a site ban after continuing to edit topics related to Israel and Palestine despite already being under a topic ban, according to the ADL.

Just days after the Oct. 7 attacks, Iskandar323 removed much of the substance of Wikipedia's "Hamas" article, including materials detailing the group's antisemitism, anti-Zionism, use of human shields and child combatants, human rights abuses and more to "a far less-read companion article" titled "Criticism of Hamas." 

The ADL said that Iskandar323 left only a "brief generalized reference behind." The organization noted that while nothing had been deleted, the moving of information made it so readers viewing the "Hamas" page would no longer see the material unless they went to a subsequent page.

On Nov. 21, 2023, the same account removed around 17,000 characters of text and citations from Wikipedia's "Gaza war" page, according to the ADL. The account deleted a section of the page detailing forensic evidence of violence committed during the Oct. 7 attacks, including decapitation, torture and sexual violence. 

Two days later, Iskandar323 removed around 7,400 characters from what remained on the page, including witness accounts from Israeli soldiers and ZAKA, a first-responder organization.

"These are not innocuous edits," Greenblatt said. "These are intentional changes designed to drive a narrative, a narrative that number one, demonizes the Jewish state. That, number two, removes all context from terror incidents in general, and specifically, specifically, that sanitizes and launders what happened on October the 7th, the worst, most brutal attack on the Jewish people since the Holocaust."

The ADL said that the consequences of the biased edits go beyond Wikipedia itself, calling the platform "the foundational infrastructure for the broader online ecosystem." Wikipedia is often favored by search engines, and can be "at or near the top of search results for most substantive queries," according to the ADL.

Greenblatt said that "Wikipedia has lost trust" at a crucial time as many large language models (LLMs), such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude and AI features embedded into other products rely on Wikipedia.

ALARMING STUDY FINDS TOP CHATBOTS MORE LIKELY TO REPEAT FALSEHOODS FROM THE LEFT: ‘TRULY ASTONISHING’

Pressure from congressional scrutiny, federal inquiries and Wikipedia's own enforcement following the 2025 report appeared to lead to a significant decrease in coordinated activity among the 30-editor group, according to the ADL. However, the organization acknowledges that while "visible signs of coordination" decreased, it does not necessarily mean that it has stopped. The 2026 report states that the problematic edits are still happening, but through "quieter, subtler techniques."

A July 2026 review identified 19 active accounts that have been editing articles related to Israel and Palestine, according to the ADL. The organization said that eight of the editors had avoided sanctions despite being part of the original 30 identified in the 2025 report. These editors are allegedly using subtle techniques, such as undoing other editors' changes, hedging factual claims and rebuilding articles slowly to avoid detection.

The other 11 editors have histories with Wikipedia, despite being new to the ADL's documentation. Like those in the group identified by the ADL over a year ago, the records of these editors — some of whom have been editing the site for years — are mostly on articles related to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

Across the 229 articles where the 19 accounts overlapped, the ADL found that the 11 newly identified editors were "far more active recently" and held the most recent edit on roughly six in 10 pages.

"I think the public has come to really appreciate that Wikipedia is, in theory, this source of unbiased information, has kind of integrity to it," Greenblatt told Fox News Digital. "But when Wikipedia is poisoning the public conversation because it is enforcing the intolerance encoded in it by these editors, it's pushing the prejudiced agenda of these anonymous actors, it's no longer an unbiased source of information. It's become, actually, a weapon."

Ultimately, the ADL gave a series of recommendations aimed at the Wikimedia Foundation, policymakers, search engines and AI developers, as well as the press and the public.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

The ADL called on the Wikimedia Foundation to strengthen accountability on sensitive pages by privately verifying editors' identities, ending anonymous IP-address editing and requiring vetted editors to resolve disputes. It also urged the Wikimedia Foundation to establish a task force on antisemitic bias modeled after the foundation's 2021 intervention against Holocaust revisionism.

For search engines and AI developers, the ADL is asking for more transparency when relying on Wikipedia as a source for an answer, particularly on sensitive topics. The organization also encouraged them to consider editorial caveats based on the topic, update information and develop bias-detection benchmarks.

When it comes to policymakers, the ADL would like to see continued oversight hearings on bias and antisemitism on Wikipedia, the creation of a task force to monitor coordinated content manipulation and the development of policy options by academics, technologists, Wikipedians and civil society leaders.

The ADL is also calling on the press and the public to recognize that chatbots and AI search summaries may be relying on Wikipedia's framing, even without disclosing that. It also urges individuals and the media to verify citations and quotes on AI-generated answers.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Wikimedia Foundation for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: Why corporate America needs one playbook for a divided Washington after November
item.description: Trump's post-2018 playbook proves a Democratic Congress won't sideline his regulatory power, and data center fights are the clearest warning.
item.content:encoded:
Data center companies learned the hard way that winning Washington isn't the same as winning the country. They had the permits, the agencies and a president who warned that towns rejecting them would end up "backwards and poor." Then the neighbors showed up.

Next month's midterms set the same trap. Polls show Democrats could sweep Congress, and the temptation in every C-suite would be to mistake a Democratic Congress for a Democratic Washington.

Companies avoid that mistake when corporate communications and government affairs leaders work hand in hand. Corporate communications staff know that November's vote won't tell you what stakeholders believe about each issue that comes up in the next two years. Government affairs workers know that Congress' flip doesn't mean President Donald Trump is out of power.

DEMOCRATS THINK A BLUE WAVE IS BUILDING. HERE ARE 3 FORCES THAT COULD STOP IT

After all, voters sent Republicans packing in 2006, but President George W. Bush still ordered the surge in Iraq two months later and lifted the executive ban on offshore drilling in 2008. President Barack Obama pushed through an immigration order, the Iran nuclear deal and Title IX guidance on gender identity after Republicans took Congress in 2014. And President Joe Biden's Federal Trade Commission kept suing corporations into his final days in office.

In each case, congressional power belonged to the president's opponents while the regulatory regime stayed in his hands. And Trump's record shows that he'll use that power. After losing the House in 2018, he did not pivot to the center. He presided over a 35-day government shutdown and then declared a national emergency to fund the border wall. He will make a deal, but on his own terms, and agencies will be his strongest leverage. Any plan that assumes he will spend two years as a quiet lame duck is hoping for a president who has never existed.

LEE CARTER: TRUMP CAN STILL GET ATTENTION, CAN HE DISTRACT VOTERS FROM THEIR BILLS?

Voters haven't changed sides, either. Voting for Democrats doesn't make voters card-carrying members. The party in the White House has gained House seats just four times in midterm elections since 1900, which means even modest losses are normal. Big losses will be about the most apolitical of all issues: the economy, where the Iran war and tariffs have raised what Americans pay at every gas station and with every grocery order.

All of this means that communications and government affairs teams need to think through the stakeholders each group normally tackles alone. Data centers show what happens when they don't. When we studied the industry for Proven Media Solutions' Insider Insights report earlier in October, government affairs teams had spent years winning permits from state and federal agencies and support from elected officials at every level of government. Corporate communications seemed to have been left out of the loop until local communities — passed over for the big important players — played a key role in slowing 40% of data centers that were due to open this year.

DATA CENTERS FORGOT THE CONSUMER — AND THAT COULD COST AMERICA THE AI RACE

Data centers are the issue du jour, but here are some others that should be considered by both functions at the corporate, division and regional levels once election results are known.

Take DEI. Corporations had already long backed off on their most controversial and political aspects with relatively modest pushback, but Trump's early 2025 executive orders put the issue back in the spotlight for months. Government contractors were especially hard hit as words like "equity" were erased from websites — good for contracts but horrible for employee relations, as many felt that diversity had been traded for profit.

GOP FRESHMAN FIREBRAND TARGETS GLOBAL CONSULTING GIANT OVER 'PLAINLY ILLEGAL' DEI PRACTICES

Should Democrats call some of the large government contractors to testify about these changes, or accuse them publicly of racist behavior, lobbying or behind-the-scenes handshakes won't solve a thing. Corporate communications is going to have to build trust with all stakeholders, especially minority partners, investors and employees — through every possible messenger — before the hearing notice arrives.

Or look at immigration, where hotel chains have been under pressure over lodging ICE agents. In January, the General Services Administration removed a Minneapolis-area hotel from federal lodging programs after a Minneapolis-area franchise refused agents rooms. Weeks later, protesters occupied a Manhattan Hilton lobby over the opposite complaint.

The chains largely shook off the local controversies, often because they smartly issued statements and then went quiet, but that may be impossible once Congress is involved. It's going to take government affairs relationships with the committees and agencies, combined with corporate communications' read on customers, employees and franchise owners, to navigate these waters.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

That is why the post-election plan needs to be a single playbook, built by both teams, that maps where the company is vulnerable, where it has leverage and which of today's allies could become tomorrow's critics. Government affairs teams know the regulators, agency staff and appointees who will matter no matter who wins. Corporate communications staff know the customers, employees and communities who will judge whatever the company says. A message written for one group will be read by the other, so it has to be the same story every time.

Democrats were supposed to be irrelevant after 2004 and 2024, and the GOP likewise after 2012 and 2020 — and, allegedly, 2026. Voters who want more money in their pockets and data centers nowhere near their backyards are not changing parties, and companies that plan as if they were, will be talking to a country that doesn't exist.

A Maryland man claims that a popular weight-loss drug caused his total vision loss, leaving him legally blind.

Todd Engel, 63, was first prescribed Ozempic in 2023 to help manage his diabetes. The GLP-1 medication, which is approved to treat type 2 diabetes, is also commonly prescribed off-label for weight loss.

Approximately four months after starting the medication, Engel was diagnosed with nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION).

POPULAR WEIGHT-LOSS DRUGS FACE NUMEROUS LAWSUITS OVER RARE ‘EYE STROKE’ LINKED TO VISION LOSS

The condition, in which reduced blood flow damages the optic nerve, can cause sudden and permanent vision loss.

"I first noticed it on New Year's Eve, 2024. I had just gotten out of the shower, was getting ready to go to work. And I said to Shelley, ‘I can't see in my right eye. It's totally black. It's totally dark in my right eye,’" Engel told Fox News Digital during an on-camera interview.

"I was horrified. I was very, very upset that I couldn't see."

DOCTORS REVEAL HIDDEN DANGER FOR SOME OZEMPIC, WEGOVY USERS WITH BRAIN DISORDERS

Engel was referred for further testing, including at Johns Hopkins’ Wilmer Eye Institute. He was told he had suffered an "eye stroke," another term used for NAION.

"The blood work came back in the normal range for me. My blood pressure was fine. They said, ‘You can go back to work,’" he said.

Engel continued taking Ozempic because, according to the family's account, neither he nor his doctors knew of a possible association between semaglutide and NAION.

About 10 months later, vision loss suddenly occurred in his left eye.

"At that point in time, losing sight in both eyes, there was a tremendous amount of concern," he said.

RAPID WEIGHT LOSS ON POPULAR DRUGS COULD ‘STARVE’ THE BRAIN, EXPERT WARNS

Doctors told Engel there was no medication or surgical procedure that could restore his vision.

Shelley Engel said that medical testing did not identify another common factor beyond Ozempic. Her husband immediately stopped taking the drug after losing vision in his second eye.

"I didn't go blind — I had my vision taken from me, which was catastrophic to me and to my family," he said.

Engel has filed a lawsuit against Novo Nordisk, the Denmark-based manufacturer of Ozempic, alleging that the company failed to adequately warn patients and doctors about the potential risk of vision loss.

WEIGHT-LOSS DRUGS LINKED TO 'OZEMPIC EARS' AND OTHER COSMETIC COMPLAINTS, SURGEONS SAY

He is among hundreds of patients currently pursuing legal action against makers of GLP-1 medications, including Ozempic and Wegovy, over claims that the drugs caused NAION.

The lawsuits allege that manufacturers failed to provide sufficient warnings about the potential risks, although a causal relationship between the medications and the condition has not been definitively established.

At the time of his vision loss, Engel was working for Howard County Highways as a heavy equipment operator and truck driver.

He had worked in the field for about 40 years and held a commercial driver's license for nearly as long.

"I was extremely mechanically inclined with my hands and in my mind. I can't do that anymore, which is extremely upsetting to me," he said.

"People want to be able to retire on their own accord when they want to, not when a medical catastrophic injury such as this ... takes away your livelihood."

PEOPLE ON WEIGHT-LOSS DRUGS REPORT FINGERNAILS FALLING OFF AS RESEARCHERS UNCOVER SURPRISING LINK

Beyond losing his career, Engel said even ordinary activities he once took for granted have become difficult.

An avid reader before his vision loss, Engel said he can no longer read newspapers, magazines or books. Inside his home, he has learned to count steps to help navigate familiar spaces.

7 EVERYDAY MISTAKES COULD BE QUIETLY DAMAGING YOUR VISION, EYE DOCTOR WARNS

"I know that coming in from our parking lot, there are 10 steps ... nine going down into our basement, 13 going up into our bedroom."

Engel said he now uses a white cane to navigate outside his home and relies on his family for help with everyday activities. His four grandchildren often guide him during family gatherings.

"They will take me by my hand and talk to me: ‘Pops, three steps straight. Then we're gonna turn right,’" he said.

"For me personally, it's embarrassing. I'm 64 years old. I shouldn't need ... my grandchildren or my wife to help me get from point A to point B."

His wife, Shelley Engel, said her husband's vision loss has affected the entire family.

"It has completely changed every aspect of our lives," she said. "There is not one piece of our lives that hasn't changed or been touched by this throughout our whole family."

For Engel, some of the most painful losses involve the things he can no longer do with the people closest to him.

"I will never be able to see my wife's beautiful face again, be able to see children and grandchildren, be able to play ball with them," he said. "And that is very, very upsetting to me."

"I wake up in the dark, I go to sleep in the darkness."

Engel said that if he had been warned about a possible link between Ozempic and vision loss, he would not have taken the drug.

"Had I known, had my doctor had any inkling that this could have happened ... I'm sure he would have asked me and I would have said absolutely not," he said. "I will deal with the diabetes ... I refuse to jeopardize my eyes."

The Engels said they are speaking publicly in hopes of preventing others from experiencing the same outcome.

"Do the research for yourselves to make sure that my catastrophic injuries do not happen to you or anybody else," Engel said. "If we can help one person, then that's a pleasure to Shelley and I."

The family's attorney, Jonathan Orent, said the legal team is seeking a warning on the U.S. Ozempic label similar to information provided to patients and doctors in Europe.

"It's amazing what just a simple warning can do," he told Fox News Digital. "That's really what this case is about. It's about information."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Novo Nordisk, the Denmark-based company that makes Ozempic, has disputed that the medication causes NAION, stating that the available evidence does not establish a causal relationship between semaglutide and the eye condition.

"A causal relationship between GLP-1RAs, including semaglutide, and NAION cannot be confirmed based on the totality of data," Liz Skrbkova, head of U.S. Media and Stakeholder Relations for Novo Nordisk, told Fox News Digital.

The company pointed to an analysis of its randomized, placebo-controlled clinical trials that found very few confirmed cases of NAION and no increased incidence among patients taking semaglutide.

Novo said it continues to monitor NAION as part of its routine drug-safety surveillance.

"Novo believes the personal injury lawsuits filed in the U.S. are without merit, and we are defending them in court," Skrbkova said.

item.title: 'Heartbroken' Washington state superintendent says no consequences for girls who protested transgender runner
item.description: Camas School District superintendent John Anzalone says girls who walked off the cross country starting line in protest will face no repercussions.
item.content:encoded:
For one question, Camas School District superintendent John Anzalone chose not to answer as an administrator, but rather a father.

He has been navigating what may be the most contentious, controversial sports story in the country right now and understands the angst it has caused numerous teenagers.

That angst came to a head Tuesday when about a dozen runners from the Camas High School girls cross country team walked off the starting line when the gun went off in their race against Battle Ground, a fellow Washington state school. Why? They were protesting their male teammate competing against the females.

WASHINGTON GIRLS WALK OFF CROSS COUNTRY MEET IN PROTEST OF MALE ATHLETE, PARENTS REVEAL HOW IT CAME TO THIS

Last month, a Camas sophomore switched to the girls team midseason after finishing 76th in a boys race. He has since won a varsity meet and placed second in two others. Unsurprisingly, this has ballooned into a national story with teammates and opponents staging protests. Anzalone didn't take a side on the issue, but he empathizes with the students' plight.

"It's always hard to see when students are upset, let alone our families. And I know this issue has polarized our country for a long time, and this has probably added to that, right," Anzalone said. "And so, as a dad, it's always hard to see your own kids or any kids in the middle of something like this. And that's probably been the most heartbreaking for me, is to see certain students really kind of in the middle of this, right? They're kids. So that's been challenging, and that's always gonna be hard."

It's hard to know exactly how Anzalone or anyone involved with the school feels about the biological male competing in these meets after starting the year with the boys. They have been either neutral (Anzalone) or mute (the coaching staff) when asked about the topic. But at a meet in Arlington, Washington, last Saturday, numerous parents made their disapproval clear. And increasingly, the athletes are doing the same.

This isn't an easy thing to do. Despite most of the country supporting the separation of biological males and females in sports, the vocal minority can be vicious. A parent last week told me he didn't want to talk because "I don't want my house burned down," while one girl who protested last month said some of her friends stopped acknowledging her.

DAD BANNED FROM SCHOOL GROUNDS AFTER PROTESTING TRANS RUNNER COMPETING AGAINST HIS DAUGHTER

But Anzalone wanted to make clear that there will not be consequences for the Camas girls who walked off the line Tuesday.

"The girls are entitled to handle this however is best for them, and I was at the meet and it was peacefully done. And of course, we'll support whatever they want to do," Anzalone said. "I felt that this wasn't just about supporting and protecting (the male runner). This was really about supporting and providing that space for the girls who did walk off to do so and not feel any repercussions. And of course, some of them looked very sad. I think some of them were very conflicted. But they're also teenagers. They're still children."

Next on the Camas cross country schedule is the Greater St. Helen's League district meet on Oct. 21. A parent of one of the Camas runners who protested Tuesday said she isn't sure how the girls will proceed. But the district meet allows for only seven varsity runners from each team, meaning the male runner will very likely displace one of his female teammates.

Anzalone said there will be no action taken to prevent such a scenario.

WASHINGTON OFFICIALS WON'T BUDGE ON TRANS ATHLETE POLICY AFTER GIRL FILES SCOTUS APPEAL FOR ALLEGED ASSAULT

"As long as WIAA policy allows (the biological male) to run, and she's eligible to run, she'll continue running. Nothing's changed," Anzalone said. "We don't make political stances as a school district. We just won't, and we can't. And so, as long as the policy stands, we're going to follow the policy."

The male runner's midseason switch violated no rules. Under Washington Interscholastic Activities Association (WIAA) policy, students are permitted to compete on teams consistent with their gender identity. This could change soon, though. On the November 3 ballot in Washington is Initiative 638, which would require students in K-12 sports to compete on teams corresponding to their biological sex. A spokesperson for Let's Go Washington — the group behind the initiative — said the measure would take effect 30 days after the November 3 election (although delays in certifying the results could push back that timeline.)

Cross country season would be over by then, but I-638 would prevent similar situations from arising in the future.

Anzalone said Camas would comply with whatever rules are in place.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"I'm at a point where I have to stand by policy and by law," he said. "And like I said earlier, if those change or go in a different direction, we'll follow that."

The Camas School District issued its own statement on the matter Wednesday.

"Camas School District recognizes that students and community members hold differing views about athletic eligibility and have the right to express those views peacefully. Our responsibility is to ensure that school-sponsored events remain safe and respectful for all participants, staff, and spectators.

As a Washington public school district and member of the Washington Interscholastic Activities Association (WIAA), Camas follows applicable state law and WIAA eligibility rules. RCW 28A.642 prohibits discrimination in public schools based on gender identity and gender expression, and current WIAA rules permit students to participate in athletics consistent with their gender identity. The district does not set these eligibility standards independently.

We will continue to prioritize student safety, privacy, and well-being. We do not discuss individual students' eligibility, personal circumstances, or potential disciplinary matters."

item.title: This sparsely populated red state quietly climbed to the top of America's financial rankings
item.description: North Dakota tops Truth in Accounting's state finances ranking with a $72,300 taxpayer surplus, while 24 states can't cover all their bills.
item.content:encoded:
Of the 50 U.S. states, 24 don't have enough money to cover their bills. Meanwhile, one under-the-radar red state stands apart from the rest, according to a new analysis of state finances.

North Dakota ranked No. 1 in Truth in Accounting's 2026 Financial State of the States report, ending fiscal year 2025 with $21 billion more than it needed to pay the state's bills. That financial cushion gave North Dakota the highest "Taxpayer Surplus" in the country at $72,300.

The taxpayer surplus figure does not mean that the state's residents receive that amount of money back in their pockets at the end of the year — rather, it represents each taxpayer's share of the state's surplus under the group's methodology.

The divide between the states with surplus versus those with burden matters, especially when the economy weakens. States with stronger balance sheets have more room to weather downturns, maintain public services and meet retirement obligations, while states carrying large unfunded debts can face tougher choices over taxes, spending and borrowing when revenues fall.

THINK YOUR STATE IS EXPENSIVE? NEW DATA REVEALS WHERE AMERICANS FACE THE HIGHEST COST-OF-LIVING

North Dakota's financial position was bolstered by its Legacy Fund, a state investment fund built with oil tax revenue.

Although oil, gas and coal tax revenues declined amid lower energy prices, strong investment earnings and federal grant revenue helped offset the drop, according to the report.

North Dakota was followed in the rankings by Alaska, Wyoming, Utah and Tennessee. The five states all had taxpayer surpluses ranging from $11,400 in Tennessee to topping out in North Dakota with $72,300. Those handful of states' financial position stands in sharp contrast to nearly half the country.

The report found that 24 states did not have enough available assets to cover their financial obligations.

New Jersey ranked last, with a $162.3 billion shortfall. Truth in Accounting translates that gap into a $45,800 "Taxpayer Burden," the highest in the country. Connecticut ranked 49th, followed by Illinois, Massachusetts and California.

The bottom five states had taxpayer burdens ranging from $16,000 in California to $45,800 in New Jersey.

THE RED STATES CHARGING AHEAD WITH AMERICA'S WEALTH AS RIVALS WATCH BILLIONS SLIP AWAY

Long-term retirement obligations are a major source of pressure on state finances.

Across the country, states had $775 billion in unfunded pension liabilities and $490 billion in unfunded retiree health care obligations in fiscal 2025, according to the report.

Despite those shortfalls, most states improved financially in 2025. Strong investment returns boosted pension assets and helped reduce unfunded pension obligations, though Truth in Accounting cautioned that those gains can reverse when markets fall.
